heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Bambu PAHT-CF exceptionally well but strictly requires upgrading the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears to hardened steel before printing. Once upgraded, it safely prints up to 131 mm/s governed by an 11 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate or Engineering Plate + Bambu Liquid Glue / PVP Glue Stick as a release interface
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 11 mm³/s in the Filament Settings to cap speeds safely at 131 mm/s for a 0.2mm layer height.
Lower Part Cooling Fan to 0% threshold and cap maximum fan speed at 20% to prevent layer delamination and severe warping.
Enable a 5mm outer brim with a 0.1mm brim-to-object gap to combat corner lifting under high chamber thermal stress.
Set the nozzle temperature to 285°C and bed temperature to 98°C, keeping the P1S front door and top glass lid fully closed throughout printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough surface finish, severe stringing, and loud popping sounds during extrusion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excess moisture absorption; PAHT-CF is extremely hygroscopic and hydrolyzes in the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in a dedicated filament dryer or the P1S heatbed chamber at 80°C for 8-12 hours before printing, and print directly from a dry box or sealed AMS with fresh desiccant.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Part warping and corner lifting off the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Inadequate bed temperature or insufficient bed pre-heating causing high thermal contraction stress at the base.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set bed temperature to 98°C, apply Bambu liquid glue stick evenly across the textured PEI plate, and pre-heat the enclosed chamber for 15-20 minutes prior to starting the print.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking, severe under-extrusion, or nozzle clogs mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive carbon fibers wearing out the stock stainless steel nozzle/gears or particulate clogging a 0.4mm orifice at lower extrusion temps.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Replace both the nozzle assembly and extruder gears with Bambu Hardened Steel components and ensure hotend temperature is set no lower than 285°C.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PAHT-CF on the P1S with the stock stainless steel nozzle and gears?
faq.answer: No. The carbon fiber fill is highly abrasive and will rapidly erode the stock stainless steel nozzle aperture and extruder drive gears within a few hundred grams of printing. You must install Bambu hardened steel components.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped at 131 mm/s when the P1S can run at 500 mm/s?
faq.answer: PAHT-CF has a high melt viscosity and an effective volumetric flow limit of 11 mm³/s. With a 0.4mm nozzle, 0.42mm line width, and 0.2mm layer height, 131 mm/s reaches that flow boundary; exceeding it causes severe under-extrusion.

faq.question: Can I feed PAHT-CF through the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, Bambu PAHT-CF is formulated to be AMS-compatible. However, prolonged use of carbon-fiber filaments will wear AMS funnels and internal PTFE tubes faster, and the filament must be thoroughly dry to prevent brittle snapping inside the feeder paths.

faq.question: Should I keep the P1S glass lid and front door open or closed during printing?
faq.answer: Keep both the glass top lid and the front door completely closed. PAHT-CF requires a hot, draft-free chamber to prevent rapid thermal contraction, residual internal stress, and premature layer delamination.
